lead.headline: Houthis seize Yemen's Red Sea coast as Saudis shut oil pipeline
lead.dek: Crude tops $100 a barrel after rebels take the Bab al-Mandeb islands; Riyadh says drones came from Iraq
body: Houthi fighters completed their takeover of Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline and the Bab al-Mandeb strait's islands Friday, while Saudi Arabia suspended its cross-country East-West crude pipeline following drone attacks, pushing international oil prices above $100 a barrel.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the operation expelled Saudi-backed forces from six districts covering 5,400 square kilometers and declared that "maritime navigation is safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels." The Saudi Energy Ministry said the pipeline, the kingdom's main export route avoiding the Strait of Hormuz, was suspended as a "precautionary measure."

About 12% of the world's goods typically move through Bab al-Mandeb, AP reported. Iraq said Saturday its prime minister had dismissed the military commander in Maysan province after finding the attacks were launched from there, and Iran said it will meet Gulf states in Oman on Monday on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. diesel passed $6 a gallon Friday.

briefs.headline: Prosecutor leading DOJ 'grand conspiracy' probe resigns
briefs.summary: Joe diGenova, named in April to oversee the probe of Obama- and Biden-era officials and a separate case against ex-CIA chief John Brennan, quit Thursday with no charges filed.

briefs.headline: Appeals court keeps block on USPS mail-in ballot restrictions
briefs.summary: The 1st Circuit refused Friday to lift an Aug. 31 injunction against a Postal Service rule limiting who gets mailed ballots; the administration has asked the Supreme Court to step in.

briefs.headline: Consumer prices rise 3.4% over the year as gasoline climbs 27.4%
briefs.summary: The August CPI rose 0.4% for the month, with gasoline up 3.9% and energy up 16.3% from a year earlier, BLS said Friday; the Fed meets Wednesday with core prices up 2.4%.

briefs.headline: Cyclospora outbreak tied to lettuce ends after 12,883 cases
briefs.summary: CDC declared the outbreak over Friday with 570 hospitalizations and two deaths in 21 states, tied to Taylor Farms de Mexico iceberg lettuce recalled July 17; FDA is still tracing the cause.

briefs.headline: Philippine ferry fire toll rises to 35 as bodies recovered
briefs.summary: The coast guard said 30 bodies were pulled Friday from the burned MV June Aster off Coron, Palawan; 43 survived and 54 remain missing of 134 aboard. The cause is under investigation.

briefs.headline: Sweden votes Sunday with far right eyeing first cabinet posts
briefs.summary: PM Ulf Kristersson has for the first time pledged cabinet posts to the Sweden Democrats if his bloc wins Sunday's general election; polls show the left opposition's lead has narrowed in the final days.

briefs.headline: Russian strikes kill 11 across Ukraine as Odesa hit overnight
briefs.summary: Local authorities said 96 were injured over the past day, at least 35 of them in Odesa; the Air Force said Russia launched 129 drones, eight Kalibr and six Kh-59/69 missiles overnight and 110 targets were shot down.

briefs.headline: Nigeria's parliament suspends official visits to South Africa
briefs.summary: Lower house spokesman Akin Rotimi said Friday the National Assembly halted all visits over attacks on Nigerians; a junior foreign minister said at least 98 Nigerians have been killed there since 2022.

briefs.headline: Wood County residents sue Chemours over landfill PFAS leaks
briefs.summary: The proposed class action, filed Sept. 4 in federal court, says PFAS leaked from a Chemours landfill near Washington Works in 2024 and 2025 and seeks medical monitoring and cleanup. Chemours has not responded.

briefs.headline: Trump signs Justice's Medal of Honor monument bill
briefs.summary: S. 858, the Hershel "Woody" Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act, signed Thursday, clears a privately funded monument to Medal of Honor recipients on the National Mall's Reserve.

briefs.headline: CAIR asks WV police to investigate threats to mosques
briefs.summary: The Council on American-Islamic Relations said Friday a Facebook post threatened West Virginia Muslims and listed mosque locations and a South Charleston school, and asked for more police presence at mosques.

briefs.headline: Attorney general probes card fraud reports in Cross Lanes
briefs.summary: The AG's Consumer Protection Division is investigating complaints of unauthorized charges at several retailers, WSAZ reported Thursday; many came from Kroger shoppers on Big Tyler Road, and no skimmer has been confirmed.

regional.item: DEP will investigate after runoff from Nscale's Mason County data center site flooded a neighboring yard Thursday for the second time.
Charleston bids the Capitol Connector on Kanawha Boulevard within weeks, turning $1.5M in city money into more than $27M federal.
Morrisey spoke at Parkersburg High Friday as it marked 25 years since 1992 graduate Mary Lou Hague died in the South Tower.
Carnifex Ferry Battlefield State Park stages a reenactment of the 1861 battle Sunday at 1 p.m., its 165th anniversary.

away.item: U.S. 7 closes fully between Exit 2 in Bennington and Exit 3 in Arlington from 7 a.m. Sept. 19 to Oct. 3 for Sunderland culvert work.

hotspots.item: A new Cowen Volunteer Fire Department firehouse could break ground this spring, The Webster Echo reported Sept. 8, as the town seeks grants for it.
Hughes Road at Center Drive in Pender County is closed from 9 a.m. Friday to 6 a.m. Monday for culvert replacement, with a detour via U.S. 17.

briefs.headline: Nine run for mayor, 19 for council as nominations close
briefs.summary: Nominations closed at 4 p.m. Friday with nine mayoral candidates, including incumbent Simon Yu, and 19 for eight council seats. Withdrawals close Sept. 18; voting is Oct. 17.

briefs.headline: Fort St. John gang sweep ends with 26 arrests, seven guns
briefs.summary: B.C.'s anti-gang unit said 26 people were arrested and seven guns and $16,000 seized Aug. 21 to Sept. 5 after three shootings. A northern gang team launches in Prince George this year.

briefs.headline: Teresa Wat gives breakaway B.C. party its sixth seat
briefs.summary: Richmond-Bridgeport MLA Teresa Wat joined the unnamed party of ex-B.C. Conservatives under interim leader Peter Milobar. It becomes the third-largest caucus when the house sits next month.

briefs.headline: B.C. judge halts extradition over DEA conduct in Canada
briefs.summary: B.C. Supreme Court Justice Catherine Murray stayed a Canadian's extradition, finding U.S. DEA agents led him into a money-laundering plot behind the RCMP's back. The April 1 ruling was posted this week.

briefs.headline: Alberta launches $4M ad campaign on referendum questions
briefs.summary: The Smith government's ads urge Yes on nine Oct. 19 questions and a 'sovereign Alberta within a united Canada' on separation. NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi called the spending unethical.

briefs.headline: Stellantis signs MOU to sell idled Brampton plant to Roshel
briefs.summary: Stellantis signed a memorandum with armoured vehicle maker Roshel on a possible sale of the plant idled in 2023, when more than 2,000 were laid off. Unifor paused talks; its contract ends Sept. 20.

briefs.headline: Cell therapy cuts fractures in small osteoporosis trial
briefs.summary: Ten women given one infusion of their own sugar-modified marrow cells went from a fracture every year or two to about one a decade, a University of Murcia-led team reported Sept. 11 in Cell. The trial had no control group.

briefs.headline: Immunotherapy regimen lifts lung cancer event-free survival
briefs.summary: Phase 3 IMpower030 data presented Sept. 12 in Seoul put median event-free survival at 62.8 months with perioperative atezolizumab plus chemotherapy, against 34.9 months for chemotherapy alone; the trial missed its significance threshold.

briefs.headline: Rocket Lab challenges NASA Mars orbiter award at GAO
briefs.summary: Rocket Lab filed a protest Sept. 11 with the Government Accountability Office over NASA's $700M Mars Telecommunications Network award to Blue Origin, saying it ignored eligibility criteria set by Congress.

briefs.headline: Rare cortical neurons help push the brain into sleep
briefs.summary: Sst-Chodl cells, about 0.2% of cortical neurons, synchronized brain activity and made mice fall asleep faster when activated, an Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai-led team reported Sept. 9 in Nature.

briefs.headline: Fields medalists rebuke AI labs' race on famed math problems
briefs.summary: Twenty-five Fields Medal winners signed an open letter saying AI labs' rush to claim solutions lacks documentation and attribution, TechCrunch reported; OpenAI pulled its sponsorship of a Caltech math event Thursday.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers push AI safety bills after researcher's exit
briefs.summary: Reps. Josh Gottheimer and Mike Lawler introduced the Stop Rogue AI Act Wednesday, and Sen. Ted Cruz said he is drafting a catastrophic-harm bill with Sens. Thune and Klobuchar, after Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic over extinction fears.

briefs.headline: AI agents plow through simulated animals to save fuel
briefs.summary: In the HarvestBench preprint from Compassion Aligned Machine Learning and the University of Warwick, kill rates across nine models ranged from 0.4% for GPT-5.6 Terra to 98.8% for GPT-4o mini, The Register reported.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore has the forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Summers County ran no regional line; WV MetroNews sat behind a challenge page all morning, and the Topsail Beach hens vote still has no posted result.
